manipCheckOpen_T: Today I read about the patient’s perspective when it comes to their health care provider.
sayingTreatment:
It is of the utmost importance that you look at and treat your patient as a family member or as someone looking into the mirror. Yes, YOU. Treat your patients how you expect and want to be treated. 

Learn who they are, not just their diseases or maladies. Learn about what makes them happy and what kind of lifestyle they have. Learn about help they have or may not have. Keep in mind that you are not just a number to your patient, and your patient should never be just a number to you. 

Some patients are easy and malleable. However, there will be times when your patience is tested. Good! How you treat the patient in these trying times speaks to who you are as a medical professional. You’ll notice that I didn’t say what you are as a medical professional. That’s because you are a human being; not a what, but a who. Treat every patient with that in mind and it will make all the difference.

valuesOpenTreatment_3: Empathy is essential in my nursing practice. This helps me to build a connection which fosters trust and understanding. Patients are often terrified, alone, and overwhelmed. I treat all patients as I would want those whom I love the most to be treated.
ypTreatment1: It is critical to understand patient's perspectives as this will allow the healthcare team to tailor the plan of care. It takes all aspects of the patient's life in consideration. There are many and sundry reasons why patients develop unhealthy habits, do not seek care, and/or are non-compliant. It is essential to tap into what has caused a patient to do things a certain way.
ypTreatment2: Many times I feel that providers are dismissive and/or outright judgemental. They can be short with patients or give the impression that they are hurrying them along. Many patients are intimidated by medical professionals and they do not feel confident asking questions or requesting clarification.
ypTreatment3a: It enhances patient care when a provider can verbalize the sentiments of the patient. It assists in repore. This allows the patient to feel as though they are on the 'same page' as the provider.
ypTreatment3b: The patient will feel heard. Care will be individualized allowing the patient to feel involved and as if the provider actually cares about their outcome.

sayingTreatment:
Welcome to the rewarding and often complicated world of medicine. 

You will see a myriad of patients with varying levels of medical knowledge. This is where you will deliver possibly the most important service you can provide, in teaching. Learn about your patients, this will help immensely in creating a comprehensive care plan that they will adhere to. Talk to them, not at them. Hear what they have to say. You will be their advocate. Ask yourself daily, how would I treat the person I love the most, what would my plan of care look like? Then execute it as if the person, who you love was seated in front of you.

Invite questions 
Teach, do not lecture
Do not judge
Listen 
Involve family
Offer viable options and small measurable goals
Be encouraging 
Share a personal story, which will help humanize, in a time where patients are scared and/or intimated
Most of all, be empathetic. 

You will see patients from all walks of life. Please treat them with the utmost respect, devoid of judgement. Their very life depends on you. 

Good luck and God speed.

valuesOpenTreatment_3: Empathy is an important value to have as a Registered Nurse because we see patients at some of the worst times in their lives when they are vulnerable, scared, and hurting in some way whether physically/psychologically or often times both.  It is important to remember as humans we all experience suffering and often times need validation of our experiences, education on the unknown, and knowing someone is there with us through this time and that's the role of the nurse, to say I see you are suffering, and I am here to help you through that, whatever that means to you.
ypTreatment1: By taking the time to listen to our patients perspectives we can provide patient-centered care that focuses on what the patient sees as a priority.  By focusing our care on the highest needs of our patient we start to establish trust and can engage in shared-decision making.  When decisions are shared and prioritized with patient's needs in mind, patients tend to increase adherence to the plan of care and patient outcomes and satisfaction improves.
ypTreatment2: In my experience, some reasons patients or families may be anxious or hesitate to ask questions is because 1. they don't speak the same language and this creates a barrier to communication effectively and efficiently at times, especially depending on communication services available. 2. Another reason is due to time constraints, provider has limited time and patient feels rushed, they may not be made to feel like a priority. 3.The patient or family member may not know what to ask because they do not know what is important or 4. they are unfamiliar with the US healthcare system and or the 5. unfamiliar with diagnosis, limited understanding of medical terminology or use of medical facilities. 5. Sometimes patients and family members are in shock depending on the medical situation and they may not be cognitively able to even process what is happening never-mind know what questions to ask, they may feel overwhelmed and have sensory and information overload.
ypTreatment3a: Understanding a patient's perspective will have a positive effect on patient adherence to plan of care.
ypTreatment3b: When the patient feels heard and respected which helps them trust their provider, the patient will increasingly adhering to a plan of care which is likely designed to improve patients health and get patient back to whichever goal they originally set together. It's a win-win for both.
ypTreatment4: It has been beneficial to engage the patient in shared-decision making when it comes to their goals as it builds trust between the provider and patient and sometimes we have limited time to build that trust.  Patients are much more likely to engage in behaviors that will complete the goals if they are driven by their own wants and needs and they feel they have support and are not alone.  A nurses role is much of the time educating, supporting, and guiding our patients to the best course of action based  on their wishes, values, and needs. increased patient satisfaction is also likely when the patient provider relationship is based on trust, utilizes active communication, and shared decision making.

sayingTreatment: It is important you understand as healthcare providers we provide care to our patient and it's up to them to decide if they want to use it.  Please listen to your patients, from day one.  Listen to their story, it will give you the answers to what they value most, what is most important to them, and it will establish trust in your relationship. Take the time to listen to your patients and ask them personal questions about themselves and their families and who they are.  In listening to their story you will identify key details to their health journey and what they value the most which can help us as healthcare providers guide our patients to the best avenue for them to receive the care that is in alignment with their needs and wants.  It is not our job to make decisions for our patients, it is our job to provide them with the knowledge, support, and the resources they need to make the best decision for themselves.

valuesOpenTreatment_3: I believe and each motivational interviewing and ways to address psychosocial issues dealing with chronic illnesses
ypTreatment1: Lots of medical problems involve patient compliance. However, this must be balanced with learning issues, sufficient time from the medical team to interact with patients in a positive, empowered, motivational interviewing style to share informaton about their illness, share their key role as a family member or as the patient and to help them understand their own needs, barriers and address how these can work together to make them healthier, take the appropriate decisions about their lifestyle, take medications corretly and improe their own outcomes. un
ypTreatment2: Too little time from HCP with patients. HCP always in a rush to see next patient, order tests, write prescriptions and too little time to use empowerment and motivational interviewing available to engage with the patient in an age-appropriate, social and family-friendly manner. To little contact with fathers or other family care-givers (grandparents, older siblings). Too little attention to providing knowledge in a less frightening and less burdensome manner.  Too little attention to open discussions about such issues to ease tensions, help understand what needs to be done by the patient/family and help assist the steps to make progress.
ypTreatment3a: Have done self-efficacy studies with adolescent diabetes patients and lectured about these as well as published. Have lectured about empowerment and motivational interviewing with chronic pediatric, adolescent and young adult diabetes and endocrinology disorders and taught these topics in 65 countries to date. Have used group teaching, individual teaching and multidisciplinary team approaches successfully to improve care, understanding, compliance as well as improve lab outcomes as well as decreased hospitalization/emergency room visits as well as improved long term health outcomes. Also have taught this in low-resource and middle-resource systems with excellent response and results.
ypTreatment3b: Helps to have HCPs understand learning needs, how to motivate and encourage open discussions and not just "giving orders" which then aren't often followed, improves understanding and then adherence/compliance also improves even with difficult tasks with both acute and chronic conditions.  Better for patient and family. Better for HCP because goals are easier to achieve so more satisfaction and less stress on both sides.
ypTreatment4:
Open-ended questions and not rapid orders are key.  Discussing psychosocial factors, financial factors and opening up discussions means having a unified multidisciplinary team approach that is internally consistent, utilizes the same empowering style of interactions and allows patients/family members to feel safe and more open about problem discussions, questions or worries while learning in a style that works for them. 
 Needs more time than most HCPs in USA and around the world typically have available to them so needs a different style approach from the healthcare system.  Can be done individually, with whole family, as well as with patient group teaching or even several family-group teaching especially applied to weekend or evening support sessions using the same useful empowerment and motivational interviewing and sharing style.
manipCheckOpen_T: Intriguing presentations about what my entire healthcare life has focused on:  patient/family/HCP interactions that promote improved knowledge sharing, compliance, adherence, short and long term healthier outcomes.
sayingTreatment: The best health care providers use empowerment and motivational techniques to help share information that is often complicated, scary and hard to follow because of learning difficulties, reading or math difficulties or other psychosocial issues. Too often patients and their families are too scared or unsure that they can express their questions or concerns and they often end up with compliance and adherence issues because the HCP is stuck with old-style autocratic sharing of information in too little time to promote open discussions about such issues.  By not simply telling people what you as a HCP have learned they should do but empowering the patient and family participation in the process, outcomes improve, compliance and adherence issues can be better addressed openly and without anger or frustration by HCPs to solve many of the short and long term issues of delivering medical information and having fewer problems n the process.

valuesOpenControl_1: My personal pc is my information hub.  Email is my preferred tool to communicate with patients/peers.  I am very careful with the amount of my "social" accessibililty.
ypControl1: I have made a very purposeful decision to remain relatively low tech.  I do have a personal pc that I use for most of my communication.  I had a cell phone when it was required for work, but got rid of it the moment I felt I could.  Constant access is problematic, in my view, I know many will disagree, but I find access all the time to be detrimental to my mental health.  In rare cases of true emergencies, people know how to reach me.  I have owned a tablet and a laptop as well.  Both have come in handy when I am unable to access my pc, but neither can fully replace the pc's utility.  Otherwise, the most up-to-date piece of technology I have is a firestick to stream a movie during down time.
ypControl2a: I have used messenger when e-mail proves to be too cumbersome to communicate with friends/colleagues that are far away.  Otherwise, I prefer to meet face to face.
ypControl2b: I don't feel they do improve communication in everyday life.  Messenger is problematic because you can't see body/facial reactions.  Phone communication shares the same problem.  Email is problematic because you can't have a flow of conversation.  Video calls are problematic because they require both parties to have the same technological know-how/savvy and access to required hardware.  Every sort of replacement tech meaning to "improve" upon face to face interaction is inferior; necessary at times, but still inferior.
ypControl3: I use my personal pc for both work and for personal entertainment.  Access to the internet allows for video gaming or viewing videos at any time, or contacting a friend for a meet up.  As previously mentioned, I also have the firestick to provide streaming entertainment whenever I desire.  That has proven to be pretty convenient.
ypControl4: I use technology to stream movies for entertainment, and I spend time reading articles to stay informed/entertained on what is happening in the "real" world.  I also have a steam account that provides gaming entertainment whenever I desire.
manipCheckOpen_C: Information was provided about how technology has influenced/changed our lives professionally and personally and how technology usage has greatly increased with time.
sayingControl: While many of the advancements regarding technology can be viewed as detrimental, occasionally it has its uses.  I am probably the last person that should be trying to convince you of the benefits of technology, but being aware of that fact may make the point a little more valid.  There are going to be times when a face-to-face meeting will simply be impossible to achieve.  Perhaps that's due to temporal differences, perhaps that's due to physical distances, or perhaps there are physical limitations that cannot be overcome.  Regardless what the reason may be, technology can serve to overcome situations in which communication may otherwise be an impossibility.  It does have its uses.  As a side-benefit, if you update your technological abilities a little bit you open up a whole new world of entertainment to access......not that we have the time necessary to really benefit from such an overwhelming library, but regardless.  Keep your mind open about the possibilities.  Yes, there are many drawbacks to constant communication/internet access, but at times, it serves its purpose as well.

valuesOpenTreatment_3: I want to treat others as I would want to be treated. It is the Golden Rule of Life. I do my best to understand where my patients come from and try to identify and empathize with them.
ypTreatment1: So I can understand better how to help them and educate them about their current medical condition and how to improve it.
ypTreatment2: The patient is too sick to be able to ask and understand what is being taught or discussed. Other patients are too busy on their cell phones to pay attention to important information. Others feel they may be judged and mistreated for questioning the care they are receiving.
ypTreatment3a: Ask the patient what works best for their lifestyle and tailor the plan of care and treatment around their schedule as best as possible
ypTreatment3b: Understanding the patient needs and home environment.
ypTreatment4: By assessing the patient needs and family and social history planning care that is tailored to their schedule and needs. Taking the time to talk to patient about their current situation and understanding of what they think is going on with their health
manipCheckOpen_T: How to better communicate with patients to provide patient centered care
sayingTreatment: Take the time to truly listen to your patients and family. Treat them as if they’re your parents or grandparents or children. Understand that they don’t have a medical background like you and need to have their medical condition explained in simple basic terms. Ask the patient what works best for them and what has not been working and how you can help them to improve their health and wellbeing on their terms.  Encourage family involvement.  Meet your patient on their level not yours. Most of all remember you are human just like your patient.
dayDetail_16: The ED is extremely busy and we are minimally staffed for nurses
dayDetail_18: I am doing my best to keep up but the wheels have fallen off the wagon and rolling down the street (it is extremely busy with. A full ED and lobby of people waiting to be seen)
dayDetail_19: It is still busy and the ambulances are rolling in and out . I need to go to the bathroom but I just don’t have the time.
dayDetail_20: Still busy caring for patients still running around and still have to go to the bathroom but just. can’t.  It gets very frustrating not having adequate staff to care for our patients
dayDetail_21: Oh well , 6 people who were checked in to be seen have left without being seen. I guess it wasn’t an emergency.
dayDetail_22: Well now things are getting better patients are getting moved to another facility, admitted or discharged so now we can see light at the end of the tunnel. I feel awful that 6 people walked out without being triaged and I am sure our Director of Nursing will be very unhappy about that. But what do you expect when you can’t give us enough staff?
dayDetail_23: I actually got to go to the bathroom finally and attempt to ea bit to eat.
dayDetail_24: Finally everyone except for a few patients are gone we succeeded to survive the craziness of the early evening
dayDetail_25: Still calm and chilled . I guess I will go do the housekeeping job and clean rooms because this place is too cheap to pay for a house keeping staff anymore during the night. They didn’t tell me I would be doing housekeepings job in addition to my nursing job when I was hired on last year.
dayDetail_26: Still calm only 3-4 patients waiting for transfer.
dayDetail_27: Oh there goes the calm now an ambulance comes in with a patient with a blood glucose of 25 to 35 not good. But the patient is awake and talking. Nice older gentleman  hard to believe he is so alert with such a low blood sugar.
dayDetail_28: Ahhh there is the dayshift coming in.. report given and time for this nurse to go home to sleep.  What a crazy night it has been dealing with belligerent drunks, angry inmates an impatient patients. I love my job as a ED nurse!

manipCheckOpen_T: How health care providers can work to ensure patient care, trust and improve care
sayingTreatment: Nursing is hard work everyday. Nursing is seeing people at their worst and most vulnerable and many of them are so frightened that they will not treat you well.  Many will lash out at out due to their fear, you will initially take this response personally because all you want to do is help.  They are rejecting you and will want to reject them.  But you will find that just as you might comfort a small child, so you will reach out to comfort your patients.  Many times this means just sitting quietly next to them, letting them know that you are there; available.  In your busy work the number of patients that you are assigned will feel overwhelming and it is.  There will not be time to do the kind of job you want to and you will be pulled away from those that need you because there are others that need you too. You will struggle with wanting to do the job you were educated to do and not being able to do it.  The most rewarding parts of nursing are often the same parts that you will not have time to do.  Your job will be filled with required tasks.  As you learn the workflow you will come to find a way to begin to meet these needs but not everyday and not for every patient.  You may want to quit.  But if you do, there will be many less nurses to care for the patients and less time that they will have to meet patients needs.  Do the best you can.  You are a success everyday that you come to work. You are doing the best that you can and will continue to work to improve your skills and help as many patients as you can.  You can reach out to others on the unit and there are also employee assistance persons that can help you to manage the personal stress of the work environment.  Best wishes.

valuesOpenTreatment_3: It is importance to treat the whole person. No one is cut from a cookie cutter mold, so healthcare/nursing care should not be as such. If you don’t get to know your patients and their circumstances then you can’t really treat or help them. For instance, what is their home life like. Is Joe a single dad taking care of his two teenagers and his employer paid insurance deductible is so high that he is still paying out of pocket of his medications. This person is not going to buy expensive new prescriptions if that means he can’t put food on the table for his kids, but the nurse won’t know that if they don’t get to know their patient.
ypTreatment1: If you don’t understand the patient and their circumstances then you won’t fully understand the patient. If a patient has to choose between feeding their children or paying for a medication most will choose their children. This does not make the a bad patient, rather they are a good parent in a tough position. As nurses we should be prepared to help them find community resources and help them to navigate our broken healthcare system.

sayingTreatment:
Welcome to healthcare! Now forget everything you were “taught” about interacting with a patient. 
Patients are not all the same, so don’t treat them that way. Everyone deserves to be looked at individually and listened to, no two people are alike. Think about it, if you have a sibling, I’m sure you hate being told you are just like so and so. If you don’t have a sibling ask sunshine that does. 
In order to earn a patients respect and trust, learn about their home life. This will tell you everything you need to know; I.E. can they afford this expensive meds the drug reps push on you, can they afford labs every 3 months or can some be done every 6, do they have transportation, do they have to choose food over meds. 
Good luck

sayingTreatment:
Please understand that you are a team member in the patients life. You are not above them, you are with them. Understand that they put trust in you. It is your responsibility to keep that trust by open communication, understanding them as an individual. If there js question, the patient can clarify.

Each patient has their own history which influences their thoughts. Please listen and acknowledge there is a lot that you don’t know. There is a lot they don’t know. This is why you meet.

I watch doctors treat people the same from patient to patient.. they tend to pass the feelings of the difficult patient onto the next patient. Don’t become desensitized.

Here is an example, I rarely go to the doctor. I went to the express clinic because I could not breath. I was told it was muscle skeletal. He didn’t listen. And to add, assessment documented did not happen.

Tuesday I called my regular doctor and got in Wednesday am. He didn’t listen. He called me anxiety. He sent me chiropractor later that day. At this time, I was defeated.

Back to the chiropractor on Friday. He listened and understood. He sent me back to a different doctor and through testing, I was diagnosed with bilateral pulmonary embolism that were extremely close to irreversible damage.

It took 2 desensitized providers to get me to the chiropractor that listened. The chiropractor listened and trusted. He sent me to a provider he knew would listen. There was zero reason for me to be called anxiety. I don’t go to the doctor. I didn’t create their minimization and desensitization. They CHOSE to pass that along. And being a nurse, I lost trust. The minimization caused by desensitization nearly caused my life. 

To new doctors- patients come in as individuals. They don’t come as a whole group of your past challenging patients. Hear your patients and listen to your patients. If for no other reason, do it because it’s your job. Yes, you are in an elite field. Yes, you make the calls. But also know, yes, you can make errors. When the patient (like myself) link errors to simple communication, the error becomes more. 

As a nurse and as a patient, I will not trust the early providers. Not because they made an error but because prior to the error, they didn’t see me as a person. The damage in relationship can’t be replaced

sayingTreatment:
Welcome the wonderful world of healthcare!
One of the most important aspects to your role will be establishing a connection with your patients. Establishing that connection can be as easy as setting down with a patient and finding out their personal stories. Jot down notes about those stories and follow up with them at each encounter. Simply asking "what is on your mind today" can let the patient know you are genuinely concerned about them. Seeing health from their perspective can make your role much more satisfying. Not all patients want the treatment plan you have in mind, find a plan that works for them!

ypTreatment2: They don’t want to “bother” anyone. They are overwhelmed. They’re scared.

manipCheckOpen_T: I read about understanding pts perspectives and having empathy, building positive relationships with patients.
sayingTreatment: Thank you for joining this truly fulfilling yet challenging field. We need more HCPs who are easy to talk to, personable, caring, empathic, kind and professional. There will be days you question why you became a HCP. Think about what your “why” is. What drove you to this field? Try to remember this during shifts when you feel burnt out, discouraged, experience compassion fatigue. And please please please make self care a priority. When you feel that your own cup is filled, it becomes so much easier to show empathy and authenticity in forming positive relationships with your patients. If you think of empathy like having a limited pocket full of coins, and each day you spend the coins. Eventually there are no more coins to give and that means it’s time for you to take better care of yourself. This is a difficult and often thankless career, but you have idea the impact you make in the lives of others. Some will remember you for a lifetime. Live by your values, remember your why, and show compassion to yourself too.

sayingTreatment: Thank you for joining this truly fulfilling yet challenging field. We need more HCPs who are easy to talk to, personable, caring, empathic, kind and professional. There will be days you question why you became a HCP. Think about what your “why” is. What drove you to this field? Try to remember this during shifts when you feel burnt out, discouraged, experience compassion fatigue. And please please please make self care a priority. When you feel that your own cup is filled, it becomes so much easier to show empathy and authenticity in forming positive relationships with your patients. If you think of empathy like having a limited pocket full of coins, and each day you spend the coins. Eventually there are no more coins to give and that means it’s time for you to take better care of yourself. This is a difficult and often thankless career, but you have idea the impact you make in the lives of others. Some will remember you for a lifetime. Live by your values, remember your why, and show compassion to yourself too.

sayingTreatment:
Empathy is absolutely crucial as a healthcare provider, especially as a new one. It's all about understanding and connecting with your patients on a deeper level. When you show empathy, you're able to put yourself in their shoes and truly grasp their experiences, emotions, and concerns.

By being empathetic, you create a safe and supportive environment for your patients. It helps build trust and rapport, which is essential for effective healthcare. When patients feel heard, understood, and cared for, it can greatly enhance their overall experience and even contribute to better health outcomes.

Empathy allows you to provide personalized care that is tailored to each individual's unique needs. It helps you communicate effectively, not just through words, but also through non-verbal cues and active listening. This can make a world of difference in how patients perceive their treatment and how well they adhere to 

So, as a new healthcare provider, remember that empathy is not just a nice-to-have quality, but an essential one. It will not only benefit your patients but also contribute to your professional growth and satisfaction.

ypTreatment2: There can be various reasons why patients may feel anxious or hesitate to ask questions. ypTreatment3a: Understanding a patient's perspective can have a positive influence on me and my recommendations by allowing me to provide more personalized and patient-centered care. ypTreatment3b: Understanding a patient's perspective can have a positive influence on the patient and their recovery in several ways. Firstly, it helps build trust and rapport between the patient and healthcare provider, creating a supportive and collaborative relationship. This, in turn, can enhance the patient's engagement in their own care and adherence to treatment plans. Additionally, understanding their perspective allows healthcare providers to address their specific concerns and fears, reducing anxiety and promoting emotional well-being. By considering the patient's perspective, healthcare providers can also tailor treatment approaches, making them more effective and increasing the likelihood of successful recovery.
ypTreatment4: In my experience, it has been incredibly beneficial to help patients see that our goals are aligned with their goals. When patients understand that we are working together towards a common objective, it fosters a sense of trust and collaboration. It allows us to establish a shared understanding of what they hope to achieve in their healthcare journey. By aligning our goals, we can develop personalized treatment plans that meet their needs and aspirations. This approach not only improves patient satisfaction but also enhances their motivation and engagement in their own care, leading to better outcomes.

sayingTreatment:
Hey there,

Congratulations on starting your journey as a healthcare provider! It's definitely a challenging but incredibly rewarding path. I'd be happy to share some insights based on my experiences.

One important aspect of providing healthcare is understanding and prioritizing patients' perspectives. When patients feel heard and valued, it can have a profound impact on their self-efficacy and belief in their ability to improve their health. For example, I remember a patient who was hesitant to follow a treatment plan due to concerns about side effects. By taking the time to listen and address their fears, we were able to find a solution that worked for them and fostered their confidence in managing their health.

Adopting a patient-centered approach is key in building trust. Making small changes in your practice, such as actively involving patients in their healthcare visits, can make a big difference. I've seen how taking the time to explain medical information in a way that patients can understand and involving them in decision-making can greatly enhance their trust in medical care. This, in turn, leads to better engagement and improved health outcomes.

Being sensitive to the circumstances that may impact a patient's journey towards better health is crucial. Understanding the challenges they may face, such as financial constraints or limited access to resources, allows us to work together to find practical solutions. By acknowledging and addressing these barriers, we empower patients to take an active role in their healthcare, increasing compliance and promoting long-term well-being.

Remember, each patient is unique, and it's important to approach their care with empathy and respect. By prioritizing their perspectives, aligning goals, and creating a supportive environment, you can make a positive impact on their health and overall experience.

Wishing you all the best in your new role!

Take care,
Maria H

ypTreatment2: There can be various reasons why patients may feel anxious or hesitate to ask questions. ypTreatment3a: Understanding a patient's perspective can have a positive influence on me and my recommendations by allowing me to provide more personalized and patient-centered care. It helps me tailor my recommendations to their specific needs, preferences, and goals. By considering their perspective, I can make more informed decisions and offer guidance that aligns with their values, ultimately leading to better outcomes and patient satisfaction.
ypTreatment3b: Understanding a patient's perspective can have a positive influence on the patient and their recovery in several ways. Firstly, it helps build trust and rapport between the patient and healthcare provider, creating a supportive and collaborative relationship. This, in turn, can enhance the patient's engagement in their own care and adherence to treatment plans. Additionally, understanding their perspective allows healthcare providers to address their specific concerns and fears, reducing anxiety and promoting emotional well-being. By considering the patient's perspective, healthcare providers can also tailor treatment approaches, making them more effective and increasing the likelihood of successful recovery.
ypTreatment4: In my experience, it has been incredibly beneficial to help patients see that our goals are aligned with their goals. When patients understand that we are working together towards a common objective, it fosters a sense of trust and collaboration. It allows us to establish a shared understanding of what they hope to achieve in their healthcare journey. By aligning our goals, we can develop personalized treatment plans that meet their needs and aspirations. This approach not only improves patient satisfaction but also enhances their motivation and engagement in their own care, leading to better outcomes.
manipCheckOpen_T: Today I read about trust/relationships between patients and doctors.
sayingTreatment:
Hey there,

Congratulations on starting your journey as a healthcare provider! It's definitely a challenging but incredibly rewarding path. I'd be happy to share some insights based on my experiences.

One important aspect of providing healthcare is understanding and prioritizing patients' perspectives. When patients feel heard and valued, it can have a profound impact on their self-efficacy and belief in their ability to improve their health. For example, I remember a patient who was hesitant to follow a treatment plan due to concerns about side effects. By taking the time to listen and address their fears, we were able to find a solution that worked for them and fostered their confidence in managing their health.

Adopting a patient-centered approach is key in building trust. Making small changes in your practice, such as actively involving patients in their healthcare visits, can make a big difference. I've seen how taking the time to explain medical information in a way that patients can understand and involving them in decision-making can greatly enhance their trust in medical care. This, in turn, leads to better engagement and improved health outcomes.

Being sensitive to the circumstances that may impact a patient's journey towards better health is crucial. Understanding the challenges they may face, such as financial constraints or limited access to resources, allows us to work together to find practical solutions. By acknowledging and addressing these barriers, we empower patients to take an active role in their healthcare, increasing compliance and promoting long-term well-being.

Remember, each patient is unique, and it's important to approach their care with empathy and respect. By prioritizing their perspectives, aligning goals, and creating a supportive environment, you can make a positive impact on their health and overall experience.

Wishing you all the best in your new role!

Take care,
Maria H

sayingTreatment:
Hi and welcome to health care.  You will start your new position in the health care world with many new feelings and will find it hard at times,frustrating at times but you have to know that it can be so rewarding and so satisfying when you help a patient heal and recover or help them be able to deal with their health issues so that they can live a better life

Remember to be kind and caring and to sometimes just Listen to what they want to share with you so that they will open up to you so that you can help them.  Never judge where they come from, how poor or rich they are, what their beliefs are ,what their family members are like or feel, or how they look or deformities or mental issues they have.  Just be kind and empathetic and take the time to listen and look and hear what they need or what they say to you.

Always have the time and effort to involve other health professionals and services that could benefit the patients needs

Enjoy your time and efforts with each patient and all we can do is give our best efforts and time and care for each patient like they mean the world to us    Good luck to you
